evidence: the-agent-run-restores-the-file-and-restarts-rsyslog-once: manifests/rsyslog_base.pp:49-55 copy ca.pem from ${ssldir}/certs/ca.pem, which with the fixture's ssldir_override /etc/puppetlabs/puppet/ssl is the file the effect compares against (cmp -> ca-restored after the hand-appended line); the 'restarted once' half rests on line 73's comment and local change #1 (the service now subscribes to the three TLS files, current manifest line 80), so a new main PID and exactly one 'Started rsyslog.service' after the noted journal cursor is what the code produces; the action is 'true' and the effect only reads state

the-tls-directory-drifts: manifests/rsyslog_base.pp:41-47 declare /etc/rsyslog.d/tls as a directory with mode 0755; the setup chmods it 0700 and notes rsyslog's MainPID under /run/p8test-rsyslog (both declared in mutates); the effect reads the mode back with stat (the action's result on the file, not its output) and the PID file's presence, which the following check needs to show the restart through subscribe at 73-80

rsyslog-can-read-the-key-as-the-user-it-runs-as: manifests/rsyslog_base.pp:65-71 copy the private key owner syslog, group syslog, mode 0600; runuser -u syslog openssl pkey reading it is what that ownership allows, with Ubuntu's PrivDropToUser syslog and rsyslogd's process user read as context; the mismatch changes only the user to nobody, which the 0600 syslog ownership must refuse, and it failed after apply in my run
